newsitem.title: GHANA: Sale of strategic bank stake lifts Ghana bourse.
newsitem.headline: Sale of strategic bank stake lifts Ghana bourse.

text.p: The sale of a strategic 40 percent stake in Social Security Bank to an international consortium of investment institutions gave a filip to Ghana Stock Exchange on Wednesday, pushing it up in busy trading.
The Ghana Stock Exchange All-Share index rose 0.47 points to close at 358.80, the exchange's market report showed.
Social Security Bank (+50 cedis to 1,250 cedis), the main riser, accounted for 28,507,200 of the 28,584,950 shares traded. All the shares offered were bought up.

A statement from the bank, dated Tuesday, said a consortium led by London-based Blakeney Management had bought the 40 percent strategic stake for $16.6 million, wrapping up the privatisation of the bank.
Wednesday's session followed one of the exchange's quietest of the year on Monday, when just 4,210 shares changed hands. Total Wednesday offers outpaced bids by 29,391,250 to 28,756,850.
Consumer products company Unilever (+3 to 768) and Pioneer Tobacco (+2 to 140) were the other risers.
Aluworks (-55 TO 1,345) and Ghana Commercial Bank (-15 to 645) were the two declining issues.

One dealer said foreign investors hold up to 75 percent of shares on the exchange and were keeping the market going. Ghanaians, he said, were showing greater interest in money market instruments offered as part of government strategy to curb inflation.
"Money market instruments offer more attractive returns and Ghanaians are interested in having quick returns on their investments," he said.
